segments.text: Welcome to RoboDaily, your daily dose of robotics news.
I'm your host, and we're here to bring you the latest updates from around the world of autonomous vehicles, cutting-edge actuator tech, and innovative robots that are pushing boundaries - every day.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Einride and DAF partner to accelerate scale-up of autonomous electric freight."

Einride and DAF Trucks have partnered to integrate Einride's autonomous driving system, Einride Driver, into DAF's premium vehicle platform, aiming to accelerate the scale-up of SAE Level 4 autonomous electric freight transportation.

The collaboration addresses industry challenges such as driver shortages and rising operating costs by enabling safe and scalable autonomous operations focusing on repetitive tasks without human intervention.
Initial tests are planned for 2026, with full integration and commissioning expected in 2027.
This partnership will likely lead to increased investment in autonomous technology for the logistics sector, potentially disrupting traditional transportation methods.
From Humanoids Daily, "The Physical Bottleneck: Why Actuator Technology is the Next Frontier for Humanoid Robots,"
this story highlights the breakthrough of Quasi-Direct Drive (QDD) architectures in overcoming the limitations of traditional industrial robotic joints.

Researchers have developed integrated actuator solutions that combine motors, drivers, and encoders into compact systems to accelerate reliable real-world deployment, enabling next-generation humanoid platforms with low impedance, backdrivability, and precise force interaction.
These advancements address the critical issue of dynamic motion in unpredictable environments where cognitive AI capabilities are outpacing hardware advancements.
By developing QDD architectures and integrated actuator solutions, manufacturers such as CubeMars are poised to revolutionize human-robot interaction.
The compact systems facilitate faster development cycles, reduced production costs, and increased reliability in real-world applications.
This breakthrough has significant implications for the AI/tech industry, with humanoid robots expected to play a crucial role in various fields such as healthcare, logistics, and service industries.
As actuator technology continues to advance, researchers and manufacturers can expect to see improved performance, increased autonomy, and more efficient human-robot collaboration.
From Humanoids Daily, "No Fingers, No Problem: X Square Robot’s 1,816-Parcel-Per-Hour Livestream Challenges Figure".
X Square Robot recently completed a one-hour live logistics challenge, setting a new benchmark with a success rate of over 98% while sorting an astonishing 1,816 parcels per hour.
The dual-arm robotic system utilized purpose-built grippers instead of complex five-finger dexterous hands, prioritizing high-speed and cost-effective throughput over marketing-driven features.
This feat showcases the technical hurdle of using vision-based AI foundation models to process raw camera pixels and generate real-time motor torque for manipulation in unpredictable environments.
X Square Robot's emphasis on commercial practicality in hardware choices demonstrates a shift towards real-world deployment rather than flashy marketing campaigns.
The challenge follows similar formats by Figure AI and AGIBOT, further solidifying the industry's focus on overcoming technical hurdles.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Honda’s new ‘Avatar’ humanoid robot suggests the spirit of ASIMO is very much alive."
This story highlights Honda's latest breakthrough in developing a human-scale multi-fingered hand for its humanoid robots.

The company has successfully created a physically capable hand that combines dexterity, strength, and durability, allowing remote control over tasks requiring human judgment combined with robotic reach and manipulation.
Honda's researchers have achieved this by integrating various technologies such as advanced sensors and artificial intelligence into their hands.
This is made possible through years of research and development focused on enhancing the reliability and functionality of humanoid robot hands.
The result is a highly versatile hand capable of performing complex tasks like threading a needle and handling heavy objects with precision.
This significant advancement in humanoid robot design has crucial implications for making robots commercially viable and widely adopted in industries such as manufacturing, healthcare, and logistics.
As Honda continues to refine its Avatar Robot technology, it will be interesting to watch how other companies respond to this development and invest further into similar research areas.
From Planet ROS, "ROS Discourse General: Want to get involved with ROS 2? Come to Waffle".
The weekly triage meeting on Thursdays at 4:30 PM UTC via Google Meet is now open for public participation.

This initiative allows individuals to contribute to the maintenance and development of ROS 2 by quickly discussing and assigning issues and pull requests that have gone unnoticed, without any prior preparation required.
The process involves attending a meeting where maintainers present the current state of the project, identify areas in need of attention, and assign tasks to participants.
This provides an opportunity for individuals familiar with specific corners of the stack to find work to do.
The event has already seen success, attracting a growing number of contributors who can see firsthand how the project works and contribute their skills.
By participating in Waffle, individuals can help maintain and improve ROS 2, fostering a community-driven development process that benefits the broader robotics and AI industries.

Until next time, stay electrified!"
